title: Seriously impressed! Glass shine all the way around!
text:
2nd day update:
See last 2 pictures. It rained and blew a ton of dust the night after the full detail. (Of course) the first is the dirty, the last picture is after a quick rinse and dry. Although it didn't completely repell the rain it came off super ez. And shined up like it never happened with minimal effort. Crazy how good this works.
Used this for the first time today. Used as a wax to clean after doing an at home pressure wash with my foam cannon. Unfortunately I have very hard water at my house so it's nearly impossible to get it perfectly dry. There is almost always hard water spots.
I decided to try this as a finishing product and I could not believe how great it works. It's literally a mirror finish all the way around. Every surface plastic, chrome, rims and paint all shine very easily.
I used about a quarter of a bottle to detail a 2021 silverado z71 from front to back including the inside of the door trim and every surface including the external glass. Pretty impressive.
TIPS:
I used a micro fiber detailing sponge as the wet rub and it worked well.
Make sure whatever you use for the wet wipes portion stays damp. If it gets too dry it is A LOT more work. Comes off really easier if you keep the cloth/sponge damp. Not dripping wet, just hand squeeze dry it and that's about perfect.
You will notice a build up in the dry cloth, I used 2 micro fiber clothes on the body and trim and a third for the rims. Even though I used the same wet sponge for the whole truck.
The dry cloth needs to be clean to get the best shine.
Last tip, if you aren't sure whether or not you have done a surface gently wipe a micro fiber on it. If it's been armored it will slide without resistance. If not, it will feel much different.

Highly recommend this product!

title: Nice Covers, but only work for certain types of seats
text: These are very colorful and seem to be durable and well made.  They seem to fit the seats snugly.  At first I thought they weren't big enough, but they stretch, so they fit firmly and won't be loosening up.  The fact that they stretch also probably makes them compatible with slightly different sized seats.  I was disappointed that I could not use these with the seats in my car because my seats have an arm rest attached to the side of the back of the seat.  If arm rests are separate, these should work for you, but if the arm rest is part of the seat, there is no way to work around it.  Another problem is that if ever want to adjust your headrests, if you have adjustable ones as I do, the seat cover goes over the head rest and you can't get to the button to adjust it.  We never adjust our headrests and most people probably don't, so probably wouldn't be a big issue.  A final little issue is that the backs of my seats have a pocket in them for use of the passengers in the back.  The seat covers cover that pocket, so you can't get to it.  If you don't use the pockets in the back of your seats or don't have them, that won't be a problem.  Really nice seat covers, but will only work with a certain type of bucket seat.  Also there is a warning on the package that they contain material that is known in California to cause cancer, but that wouldn't be a concern to me, as I wouldn't be making any direct contact with the material and have no children or pets that would be riding on the seats.  If you often wear shorts or sleeveless shirts, you might not want your skin touching them repeatedly, because of the cancer warning.  If you don't, I wouldn't worry about it and I wouldn't hesitate to use these, if they would fit my seats.

title: Nice looking flagpole
text:
All in all it seems like a good quality flag pole. We will see later how the flag itself holds up to the constant flapping while I’m riding.
A lot of people have complained how either the flag eventually slips right off the end, or the top part unscrews and they lose both it and the flag.
There are a couple of easy solutions if you take the time to actually think about it. As far as the flag, slipping off after you screw the top piece on, you could add some stitching to make it really snugged on the pole, so it will not slip off.
An easier way is to simply get a flat washer that’s approximately the same diameter as the threaded part and put it on there before screwing the top piece on. That way there is no way the flag could slip off.
Most people that have lost that top piece, obviously didn’t think to tighten it with pliers.
I gripped the top piece and the pole with two pair of pliers, using a piece of cloth so the teeth wouldn’t tear up the chrome, and snugged it down.
It’s definitely not coming off. If you want to make doubly sure you could always put a small, very small amount of Loctite on there, but I personally wouldn’t do that. If you ever have to change out the flag, it would be very difficult to undo it without damaging the chrome.

The manufacturer of this flag pole would be smart if they simply put a flat surface on two sides of the top piece so you could use an open end wrench to tighten it down. They could also flare out the bottom of the top piece, so a flag would not be able to get past it.

I decided I wanted a 3rd one. This one is definitely the best! If I had gotten this one first, I still probably would have gotten at least one more, but I think 2 would have been suffice. This one is the longest of the three units. It's also the sturdiest. It's versatile regarding the dividers inside. The handles are sturdy. Overall, I find this to be an impressive trunk organizer.

title: Heavy Duty
text: My 19 year old daughter recently inherited grandma's car. The car was well maintained, but we were surprised that Grandma didn't have any jumper cables in the trunk. We wanted our daughter to be prepared, so I ordered this. When it arrived, I was caught off guard with how heavy it was. I wasn't expecting that at all. Then after handling, you can immediately tell the difference between these cables and others. They are truly heavy duty. The very day they arrived, my daughter went to her car to put new floor mats inside. The door wasn't opening with the key fob, so she had to insert the key into the lock. Then it was discovered that the car battery was dead. Lucky for me, this gave me the perfect opportunity to try these out. They worked as they should and as expected. The car is a 2012 Honda Civic. The reader indicated that it wasn't an issue with the alternator., which was good. Our daughter got to learn first hand how to jump start her car. When the car was up and running again, we discovered that she had left one of the overhead lights on, so of course, we had to point that out to her so she would be aware of that in the future. We were able to charge the battery overnight. All is good. The cables come with a storage bag, but it was nearly impossible to get them back in it. In fact, I don't think I did get them in properly. I guess I was thinking that I would do that later. The set included a flashlight and a pair of gloves, too. The flashlight doesn't come with batteries and it was cracked, so we'll probably just give her a different one. We compared the cables with the ones in my husband's car and they are significantly heavier, longer, and thicker. I would definitely recommend these!

title: Well....
text: My daughter has recently gotten her first car. I thought this would be great for her to have. Well......it's got a lot of stuff in it, but the items are pretty basic and some of them are poor quality. The kit comes in a storage bag. There are jumper cables, a safety vest, tire pressure gauge, safety triangle, ice scraper, screwdriver, tape, whistle and more. The safety vest is pretty light weight and cheap, but it works and will definitely draw attention to you if you were out changing a tire. The whistle is sturdy and decent. The safety triangle is a much better option than road flares, but it's wobbly. The rain poncho is cheap and probably only a one time use. The snow shovel is really more like an ice scraper. The tow hook is not very sturdy and it's questionable as to how strong it would be in use. Overall, it's got a lot of stuff, but it might be better to purchase better quality items that you will feel confident that will work in an emergency. We plan to do that for our daughter.

title: Worked Well on One of Our Cars
text: My husband's license plate got all bent up in a car wash recently. I thought this would help prevent that from happening again. He drives a Honda Civic. We started to install it with the holes at the top, but that covered up the expiration date and county. My husband didn't want to get a ticket for that. So we put it up the other way with the holes at the bottom. That worked really well. The license plate is secured with screws at the top and the frame is secured at the bottom. It came with tops to cover the screws so it's all uniform looking. We planned to put the other frame on our son's car. His plate has been bent up, too. (We think our state has been using really cheap, thin metal for tags!) Unfortunately, we couldn't use it on his car. He drives a Toyota Prius. The car doesn't have screw holes at the bottom, only at the top of where the plate goes. We tried my Toyota Sienna next. Same problem. Only top holes in my car, as well. The frame works well on some cars! If you don't want information covered by the frame and use it the way we did, make sure your car can do that!

title: Easy to Set Up!
text: We recently had a trailer hitch installed on my Toyota Sienna mini van. We thought this cargo rack could come in handy, especially with our daughter moving to college this fall. From out of the box, it took my husband less than 20 minutes to assemble. He used a socket set instead of the tools provided, which he recommends to anyone getting this. Once it was put together, it didn't take long to set it up on the van's hitch. It does require a wrench for installing it on the hitch, so make sure you take one with you just in case. There's a sleeve inside the bar that attaches to the hitch. The first time we tried hooking it up, the sleeve had slipped out a little, so we could not get the bolt to screw in because the threads weren't lined up properly. Once we discovered that, we were more careful when sliding it on to the hitch so the sleeve wouldn't slide out and we were able to get it in correctly. The hitch we have is close to the ground. This angles up a little so it leaves adequate clearance. My husband drove it around the neighborhood a few times and didn't notice any rattling or other noises, and it seemed to drive smoothly. The rack is pretty sturdy and well made. It did get scratched up a little during assembly though. Overall, we're quite pleased with it and better yet, we don't think we'll need to rent a trailer to move our daughter into her dorm. I think between this and the space in the van, we'll be good.

I got tired of those "stick" tire pressure gauges breaking and of wondering whether they're accurate or not. For less than ten bucks this is good:

PROS: Heavy duty; either side of the connector works so can use at different angles; checked it against a friend's expensive air compressor gauge and it's accurate; bleeder valve lets out air down to PSI you want; round part is encased in rubber.

CONS: Turns a one-handed job (with the stick gauge) into a two-handed job; takes up more space in a glove compartment.

Press the connector onto the tire and it pressurizes the gauge to the PSI. Then the gauge holds the reading until you press the bleeder valve on the side. I fill my tires to ~35 PSI on a 12-volt portable air compressor, then use this and bleed it down to 30. Easy every time.

title: Perfect Fit, Easy to Manage
text:
We purchased two sets of front floor liners, one for a Ford Escape and the other for a Jeep Patriot. The installation in the Jeep turned out to be much more satisfactory for the following reasons: (1) the liners are much more FLEXIBLE than the ones we received for the Escape; and (2) the Jeep uses a simple hook to hold the driver's side carpet in place. The design of the liner on the driver's side easily accommodates the hook. (See my companion review of the liners for a Ford Escape.)

Because of the flexibility of the liners and the interior design of the Jeep, it appears that the liners will be easily removable should they contain liquid or debris. They will readily go "straight up and out" of the vehicle should the need arise.

The installation of the liners in the Jeep turned out to be a much more satisfying experience than for the Escape. The liners for the Jeep give a much better measure of this product. You should be very happy, as we are, if you buy these liners for your Jeep Patriot!

title: Keeps Your Vehicle Clean (Updated June 2013)
text:
These liners cover the front carpet for both the driver and passenger sides. They are very sturdy and help to trap whatever would have wound up on your interior carpeting. They fit snugly. All very good so far.

The Ford Escape has two grommets (plastic) that normally hold the carpet in place. To install the liners, you must remove the carpet, which is easy to do. This leaves the two grommets exposed. Now the liner does have grommet holes which are supposed to match up with and fit over the two grommets. This is where matters go slightly awry: the liners that I received for the Escape are VERY stiff, so it is not very easy to position the liner holes over the grommets -- esp. the grommet farther in. I was not able to get the grommets into the holes of the liner. The holes seem a tad small. It does not seem to matter, because the liner fits very snugly and does not seem to move around at all. Since there are no grommets on the passenger front carpeting, there is no issue on the passenger side.

Because the liners I received are so stiff, I am not quite sure how easy it will be to lift the liners out and dispose of any liquid that might accumulate (e.g. snow, coffee spills, and the like). There is the possibility that in trying to remove these liners, the liquid could wind up all over the remaining layer of carpet. It does not seem that the liners will easily go "straight up and out" because of the inside dimensions of the Escape and the size of the liners.

All in all I am glad we bought them, because they are better than the alternative -- messy carpets. The liners are well made and they look good in the vehicle. I just wish they were a bit more flexible for the reasons outlined above.

title: Pump Quits Without Warning After 2-3 Months
text:
This IDEAWORKS JB4840 SIERRA TOOLS JB5684 BATTERY OPERATED LIQUID TRANSFER PUMP is extremely fast and efficient for pumping water–until it simply stops working. This has happened with all three (3) of my pumps.

The first time, I thought that the malfunction was my fault, because I had been careless about turning the pump upside down. This allows water to enter the battery compartment, so it seemed reasonable that the pump might quit due to wet connectors. After all, the instructions warn you NOT to turn the pump upside down.

The second time, I was extremely careful about keeping the pump upright. It worked longer than the first pump, but quit unexpectedly–in the middle of a job–after a few months.

The third time, the pump worked exactly like the second pump. I loved using these pumps for emptying water out of my Aerogardens, but they have to be replaced far too often. Apparently there is something wrong with the design or quality control.

The pumps cost too much (about $18.50 on Amazon) to be replaced every few months. If you decide to take a chance on this product, be sure that you have a backup siphon available to use when it quits on you.

title: Purchased to Carry in Car’s Trunk for Emergencies
text:
I ordered this FOSEAL PORTABLE AIR COMPRESSOR PUMP (12V DC, 150 PSI, Auto Shut-off; with Emergency Led Light & Long Cable; Red) to carry in the trunk of my Honda Accord for emergencies. I don’t want to repeat an incident where my car’s “Low Tire Pressure" warning light came on when I was far from any source of compressed air. (I do forget to check the tire pressure regularly.)

It’s amazing to me that this lightweight box can be an air compressor--and that it can work from an automobile’s accessory power socket. Inflating a tire with this takes only a few minutes. You just connect the pump to the accessory socket and to the tire. Then you set the desired air pressure, press the “On” button, and wait while the pump inflates the tire. The pump turns off automatically when the preset air pressure is reached.

The recommended air pressure for your tires is usually found on a sticker placed where you can read it if you open the door on the driver’s side. My first choice in a tire inflator is the [[ASIN:B015VXWZ9O JACO SmartPro Digital Tire Inflator]], but it is currently unavailable (apparently the manufacturer is readying a new model).

A portable tire inflator like this one is much easier to use than an air hose at a gasoline station. (And you don't have someone breathing down your neck, waiting to use the air hose, either.)

I haven’t owned the Foseal Air Compressor Pump for long enough to know how reliable it is, or how long it will last.

title: 12.5” Swivel Seat Is Too Small for Bucket Seat of Honda Accord
text:
This HEALTHSMART SWIVEL SEAT CUSHION (Black with Red Stripe, 12.5 Inches in Diameter) works fine as a swivel cushion for my little black folding stool; it does NOT work as a swivel cushion in the passenger-side bucket seat of my Honda Accord. Although it appears to fit the Accord’s bucket seat, it sinks down into the middle of the seat, and the flared sides of the seat prevent the cushion from swiveling.

What does work in the Accord’s bucket seat is a larger [[ASIN:B003DLXEA6 16-inch diameter Medline swivel cushion]]. The larger swivel cushion sits atop the flared sides of the bucket seat, and the cushion is able to swivel. The swivel cushion is extremely helpful to my disabled husband, when he gets in and out of the car.

The 12.5” striped HealthSmart swivel seat is a “Vivi” brand swivel seat, made in China, and “manufactured for HealthSmart International”. It seems to be reasonably well made, and the cover is machine washable. Obviously the red-and-black swivel seat is NOT a good match for the ivory upholstery of my car, but that wouldn’t matter if the small cushion were able to swivel.

In my experience, the plastic swivel portion of this type of cushion always wears out over time. The person’s weight causes the connection between the plastic swivel part and the cushion to break, or else the plastic swivel portion cracks. You can expect to have to replace any regularly-used swivel cushion from time to time.

The larger swivel cushion sits atop the flared sides of the bucket seat, and the cushion is able to swivel. The swivel cushion is extremely helpful to my disabled husband, when he gets in and out of the car.

The 12.5” striped HealthSmart swivel seat is a “Vivi” brand swivel seat, made in China, and “manufactured for HealthSmart International”. It seems to be reasonably well made, and the cover is machine washable. Obviously the red-and-black swivel seat is NOT a good match for the ivory upholstery of my car, but that wouldn’t matter if the small cushion were able to swivel.

In my experience, the plastic swivel portion of this type of cushion always wears out over time. The person’s weight causes the connection between the plastic swivel part and the cushion to break, or else the plastic swivel portion cracks. You can expect to have to replace any regularly-used swivel cushion from time to time.

title: Stopped Working.  Signal-Blocking Pouch Protects Cars With Keyless Entry Systems
text:
UPDATE: One year later, I retested this item, and it has stopped working. My car starts even though the car key fob is inside the Faraday bag. Another of these, purchased at the same time but used only to shield a second car key fob stored in a drawer, is still blocking the fob signal (so that my car won't start.) Star rating downgraded from 5 stars to 1 star, because of lack of durability and need to regularly retest for effectiveness.

This UPGRADED TICONN PREMIUM FARADAY BAG FOR KEY FOB (2 Pack) completely blocks the signal from my 2019 Honda Accord key fob. When the transmitter is inside the bag, and inside the car, the car absolutely will NOT start. Just make sure that you place the fob in the BACK pocket (the one with the white lining). The front pocket does NOT block the signal.

Keyless car entry systems (like those on the newer Hondas) make the cars that are equipped with them much harder to steal. However, thieves with sophisticated tech knowledge and equipment can enter or steal these cars by (1) hacking the fobs with signal boosting software, or (2) capturing the fob signal as the driver walks away, using special equipment developed by auto manufacturers.

If you always store your fob inside a metal box or a signal-blocking pouch like this one, you are protected from these kinds of thieves. (You definitely need to store the fob inside the pouch even when the fob is inside your home.) Other reviewers say that signal-blocking pouches stop working after a time, so be sure to test the pouch every so often to verify that it’s still working.

This pouch is large enough to easily store my Honda fob and an attached keychain charm. There’s room left over.

title: It'll Get You There . . . or Close to There
text:
There are three big reasons why I'm not crazy about my TomTom VIA 1405TM GPS navigator. First, it often plots routes requiring a lot of extra driving around, even after I've installed the latest maps. Second, the touch screen isn't very sensitive, so that an instruction to "tap" really means "press and hold". Third, the on-screen navigation displays are kind of clunky, so that extra "taps" are needed to cancel operations, select operations, and get traffic information.

ROUTES. The routes are something of a problem. A couple of actual examples: (1) When I asked for a route from one store to a nearby Safeway store (in a small shopping center), the TomTom ignored a traffic signal that allowed a left turn into the shopping center's parking lot, and routed me around several extra blocks so that I could make a right turn into the same parking lot. (2) When I intentionally went off route on my way home, the TomTom failed to adjust to my alternate, non-freeway route, and kept giving instructions for returning to the original, freeway route that was now far out of my way. It was only when I was very close to home that the instructions adjusted to take me home along the alternate route.

VOICE INSTRUCTIONS. Closely related to the routes issue is the quality of the voice instructions. Usually these tell you to prepare for turns, and to make turns, in plenty of time. However, on the freeway the voice instructions do not tell you to get out of forced-exit lanes (although the driving map shows the correct lanes), and they frequently tell you to "keep left" when all you need to do is continue on down the freeway. Maybe the voice is worried that you'll take the next exit ramp? Also, the voice instructions frequently say that you've reached your destination when your destination is only close by (perhaps a half block ahead). Worse, when you go off route by turning into a parking lot before you've reached the plotted end of your route--a good idea, since your plotted destination is often beyond the last parking lot entrance--the voice instructions become very confusing as they attempt to direct you back to the plotted route.

TOUCH SCREEN. The sensitivity of the touch screen is adequate for general navigation and plotting of routes. However, because a "tap" isn't enough, it's unwise to attempt these operations while you're driving, unless you're stopped in traffic. The main issue here, is that you can only get "traffic incident" and "delay" information by touching and holding the appropriate spot on your 3D route screen, so you'll be wanting to check this when driving. (Live traffic information is available on this model when your device is plugged into your car's power or cigarette-lighter socket).

NAVIGATION MENUS. The home screen has a "drive to" option that lets you choose a favorite, find a point of interest, or program a new address. But when you choose a location and route, you must touch the "Done" button at the lower right to reach the 3D driving map. There are many screens that require you to hit "Done" or "Back" to go elsewhere. Having to back out of screens is not only clunky, it's unsafe when you're driving (because you have to keep pressing and holding a spot on the small screen). Some nice menu features are (1) the Zoom buttons for the maps (but not as useful as they might be because the lack of screen sensitivity makes them unavailable, as a practical matter, when you're driving); (2) the "exclude part of route" option (e.g., exclude the freeway) that enables you to plot an alternative to the default route ("fastest" is the factory default setting); and (3) the "route planning" options for route types (fastest, shortest, bicycle, walking), and ferries, unpaved roads, etc. A not-so-nice feature is the ease with which you can inadvertently change your Home address or a Favorite address to something that's programmed in that isn't the correct address.

SETTING UP. Setting up the device was a little confusing for me. My Win7 computer didn't recognize it at first, although my WinXP computer recognized it right away. Perhaps the device needed some charging, perhaps it needed to be turned on. I've discovered that it may be necessary to press the "on" button several times, or to press and hold the button, to turn it on. (There's a convenient setting available that will turn the device on and off automatically when you plug it into a power source, but this is not the factory default setting.) Once you have the device plugged in, you need to go to TomTom's "get started" web site to download whatever new software and maps are available. You will have to create an account, so that you can work from "My TomTom". As I was figuring all this out, the software gave conflicting messages by saying that the device was up to date when it wasn't. Finally I learned that the TomTom device will show a "do not disconnect" warning when it is actually doing an update.

BATTERY LIFE. The TomTom VIA 1405TM display depletes the battery's charge quickly if the device is not connected to a power source (there are battery-saving options that will help with this a little). When you are driving, you will want to plug it into the car's power socket (an adapter is included, which also enables live traffic information on this model). In addition, you can charge the battery with the included USB cable by plugging the device into your computer or into a USB wall plug adapter (e.g., [[ASIN:B006GWO5WK Amazon Kindle PowerFast]]). Because of the short battery life, you will probably need a powerpack (e.g., [[ASIN:B007ZQJ5XU Incredicharge I-8800 Backup Battery Charger]]) if you plan to use this device for bicycling, walking, or bus routes. The battery icon appears on the 3D map (drive a route) display when the device is disconnected from any power source, but not otherwise.

LOCKING-SUCTION-CUP MOUNT. The device is permanently attached to a locking-suction-cup mount. You can attach the mount to your car's windshield with the suction cup, or attach the mount to the included adhesive disk (which you attach to your dashboard). Because I don't trust suction cups on windshields, and don't like having a permanent GPS mount showing in my car, I attached the mount to a portable [[ASIN:B0051FWA7U AmazonBasics GPS Dashboard Mount for TomTom]]. When locked, the suction-cup mount seems to hold quite firmly.

COMPARISON TO OTHER NAVIGATION DEVICES. The only other GPS navigation device that I own is the Verizon Navigator feature on my cell phone ($1.99 a month discounted in a special offer; regular price $4.99 a month). I think that the Verizon Navigator is quite a bit better than the dedicated TomTom VIA 1405TM device. The Verizon routes are direct (without including unnecessary extra blocks of driving); the information on bus, walking, and other alternate routes is more accessible; there is better information on nearby points of interest that are possible destinations; the navigator warns me when I've gone off route, and plots a new, efficient route immediately; the traffic lanes change color in the Navigator display to show congestion when traffic delay information is available; the voice commands are generally clearer; and the onscreen navigation is more intuitive. Although this TomTom VIA 1405TM model includes lifetime maps (you must activate the feature, using a code provided in the box), it will take many months of using Verizon Navigator before the cost of the feature will equal the cost of the dedicated TomTom GPS device. Thus a navigator app may be a better choice if you own a smartphone.

If you don't own a smartphone, the TomTom VIA 1405TM should work for you, once you get familiar with the updating, the display screens, the route plotting, and the lingo of the voice instructions. The device will reliably direct you to your destination, or at least to a point close to your destination. Because the TomTom VIA 1405TM works reasonably well as a GPS navigator, but has its drawbacks, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's OK" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Extreme Facial Closeups Only

I bought this small mirror to be able to inspect sun-damaged skin on my nose and face, in order to identify any tiny, possibly precancerous skin lesions that should be removed by my dermatologist if they should start to exhibit changes. For this purpose, the 20X magnification is perfect.

To use this mirror, you need to hold it close to your eyes and look straight into it. Otherwise you can't see a focused image. Thus it's a mirror with very limited use. For general purposes (e.g., applying eye makeup), a magnifying mirror with 5X magnification is a much better choice, because the 5X mirror will show a larger area of your face.

title: Three Gaskets, One Spring, for Repair of Leifheit Cherrymat
text:
The [[ASIN:B001MSYWQW Leifheit Cherrymat]] is great for pitting large quantities of fresh cherries, but it's somewhat fragile. The metal rod that punches the pits out of the cherries can damage a misaligned rubber gasket, or the rubber gasket can simply wear out. Apparently the spring (in the handle) that powers the punch rod can also wear out.

This Cherrymat repair kit includes three (3) replacement rubber gaskets, and one (1) replacement spring for the handle--exactly as pictured in the product photo. I'm not pleased that I needed a Cherrymat repair kit so soon, but I'm very pleased that a repair kit is available.

This repair kit ensures that I'll have a "production" cherry pitter available for home use during the full cherry season (after I damaged one of the two gaskets that came with the pitter). The Cherrymat has spoiled me, because I can prepare whole bowls of stemmed, pitted cherries in advance, and have the cherries ready for a pure, delightful eating experience.

title: Nice kit that should be in your car
text:
I got this after my car battery died and I realized my jumper cables had a tear and wouldn't work. While it probably makes sense to have a set of jumper cables just in case this doesn't work, this is the self-contained solution to jump your battery.

It comes with a nice carry case to keep everything organized too. The display on the unit shows that battery level, which is super useful when determining when you should charge. My big question is how long the unit will hold charge without being used/charged. Since the units last full charge a month ago,the battery is still at 100% (it's been kept at room temp; I'm not sure how a cold climate would affect this).

It's also really nice that you can use this to charge other electronics (phone, etc.) in the case of a pinch (though to be honest, just get a car adapter).I would recommend keeping this solely for jumping the battery if needed.

The jumper cables feel plasticky and the battery unit itself has a nice heft, but also has a little plastic feeling. That said, it works perfectly, so I won't deduct any stars for it.

I've been really impressed with this and would definitely recommend it (in addition to a set of actual jumper cables just in case!)

title: Powerful enough to jump start cars and some trucks and RVs; HEAVY
text:
This review is for the Schumacher DSR ProSeries DSR 141G 2000A 12V Jump Starter that is made in Mexico.

I have been carrying a jump starter in my vehicle since the 1990’s because I got tired of trying to find someone who would give me a jump with my booster cables every time I was stranded in a parking lot away from home. I used to own a car where the standard form of transportation was a tow. Thankfully those days are over.

This is my eighth jump starter and I ordered this because my heavy duty one that I got in June of 2017 is at the end of its life. My first two were an AC Delco and another one whose name escapes me. I also currently own a [[ASIN:B06XD6XBCM DEWALT DXAEJ14 Digital Portable Power Station Jump Starter 1400 Peak with 700 Instant Amps and 120 PSI Digital Air Compressor and two 3.1A USB Ports]] and am on my second [[ASIN:B000XQ9MGE Jump-N-Carry JNC300XL 900 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] (which is great for small tasks and jumping small cars). I also previously owned two of [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. Personally, the Jump-N-Carry (JNC) brand is my favorite and they are the ones (both the JNC300XL and JNCAIR 1700) I would carry with me all the time if I did not order this one.

Over the last 10 years I regularly carry two jump starters in my trunk. One acts as a backup (that is the JNC300XL) and is available to also charge a cell or GPS or dash cam and the other is heavy like this one and can jump several vehicles at a time in any weather.

With regard to this unit, this should be charged a minimum of 36 hours to a maximum of 48 hours before first use. It should also be re-charged every month after that. Mine arrived fully charged. This is a powerful 2000 AMPS, which is really designed to jump multiple cars, some trucks, or some commercial vehicles or some RVs in all climates without having to recharge after the first use. I personally like to have a powerful unit with me because I want to be able to get more than one jump out of it before I recharge. I’ve charged both my boyfriend’s and my girlfriend’s cars in the past with my JNC without having to recharge for a couple of months. Since I do not have a dead battery, I have not used this Schumacher to jump a car yet. However, I tested the 12V port and it worked flawlessly. I trust that this will work well to jumpstart a car or truck several times over.

Therefore, this is designed for jump starting only with the ability to charge a 12V appliance like a cell phone, GPS, dash cam, portable air compressor, 12V car vacuum, etc. There are a couple of things missing on this unit at this price point that I would have liked to have. I would have loved the addition of an air compressor and a light. This Schumacher is comparable to the [[ASIN:B01GQDBNWS JNC770R 1700 Peak Amp]] except this one has 300 more AMPS. Note that my [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 favorite jumpstart]] can sometimes be purchased for under $160 when it goes on sale. Therefore, when I say “at this price point,” I’m comparing the sale price of my favorite to the regular price of this one.

The recommended recharging time for this one is every month. For the JNC, the recommended recharge is every three months, which I like better.

In summary, this is an excellent jump starter. I have faith this will work to jump a battery even though I did not have a dead battery to test this on. In addition, the 12V port is great for charging cell phones or operating a portable air compressor. This unit is heavy and is designed for jump starting cars and some trucks, RVs, or commercial vehicles. It will be a workhorse for that purpose when paired with the appropriate vehicle. The current price of $152.99 is competitively priced. If one also needs an air compressor, then I suggest either the JNC or Dewalt I mentioned above. The Dewalt even has two USB ports. However, I just happen to love the JNC brand. It all comes down to one’s needs. If I was not so in love with the JNC, this unit would have received 5 stars from me. PS - I love the limited edition green color!

title: Not manufactured to the standards of my Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 & missing a 12 volt DC outlet but lights are excellent
text:
This is my fifth jump starter. Two jump starters from the past wore out; one of which was an AC Delco. I currently have two others that still work. A [[ASIN:B000XQ9MGE Jump-N-Carry JNC300XL 900 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] (which is great for small tasks and jumping small cars) and [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. Personally, the Jump-N-Carry (JNC) brand is my favorite over the previous two brands I tried and over this DeWalt.

I always carry two jump starters with me in case I ever have to jump start my car or put air in my tires. I also use the ones I currently own for when I need an another DC outlet to power an extra GPS or other 12V accessory. My JNC300XL is dying so, I got this DeWalt as a backup to that.

This DeWalt is comparable in power to the [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. The unit is also very heavy like the JNCAIAR 1700. Even though this appears to arrive 100% charged, I charged it for 40 hours before first use as the manual recommends. This contains a lead-acid battery, so it needs periodic charging as heavy discharges between recharges will cause loss of battery life.

The unit has:
- A backlit LCD screen
- An air compressor with hose (with ability to decrease or increase pressure and stop at a set PSI rating)
- Two 5V USB Ports
- An alternator check button (manual instructions must be followed)
- Jumper clamps for jump starting a battery
- Build-in 120 Volt AC Charger (NOTE that the AC cord is NOT provided. I use a cord similar to this [[ASIN:B007T1UUOY Calrad 55-788 18 AWG AC Extension Cord, Black, 6 Inches]])
- Two banks of three LED lights that are very bright; this is my most favorite feature
- Also supplied are a 12 Volt DC Charging Adapter and a nozzle adapter for the air hose

In addition, it comes with a one-year limited warranty.

However, I am disappointed that this unit DOES NOT have a DC outlet to power 12 volt accessories. Unless I buy some sort of converter like [[ASIN:B01J67JIOQ ARECORD USB A Male to 12V Car Cigarette Lighter Socket Female Converter]], I cannot power my GPS or attach any other 12V accessory like a car vacuum cleaner to this unit. Since I already have chargers for my phone that plug into my car lighter, I don't really need the individual USB ports because if this unit had a DC outlet, I can always use the car charger instead.

Besides this, my biggest disappointment is in the quality standard of the booster cables. As you can see from the attached pictures, both the positive and negative cables have exposed wiring. Appearance-wise this looks dangerous; it also looks sloppy but I'm more concerned about the danger. I still plan to use this unit as a backup when one of my JNC's fail; however, due to the exposed wiring (that none of my past and present jump starters have ever had) and the lack of DC outlet, this is not a unit I would buy.

I am partial to the quality of the JNC and if one is looking for a powerful jump start, my recommendation is to consider the [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]] or the [[ASIN:B000JFJLP6 Jump-N-Carry JNC660 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] first. For charging small passenger vehicles, then the lower end JNC300XL works fine and a heavy unit like the JNCAir 1700 or this DeWalt is not needed. However, the JNC300XL has a low quality light and does not have an air compressor but if one has an external 12V air compressor like I do, that unit will power it with its internal DC outlet. Besides the JNC300XL is extremely portable and compact and the one unit I had for years prior to buying the JNCAIR 1700 on sale.

title: The standard-size cover is almost perfect for my car but the magnets need to be much stronger

I have two peek-a-book holes on each side of the top of the windshield with this size so I probably should have purchased the larger size. However, since my car is a convertible, I only have the top part of the windshield frame against which I can place the top magnets. Other vehicles at least have the roof, which I do not.

The cover does adhere snugly and does keep the ice and frost off my windshield. It's both easy to affix to the car and easy to remove. One shake of the cover dislodges any ice crystals that have formed. Although the plastic is very thin it still does the job. My only complaint it that the magnets are not strong enough.

During mildly to very windy days, the top part of the cover keeps pulling away from my car and folding over so that 30% of my windshield is exposed. One day I re-seated it six times and finally gave up. However, when there's little or no wind it works like a charm.

UPDATE February 23, 2015: Branden Conn, owner of Owner Apex Automotive, contacted me about the magnet issue. They had first contacted me before I even posted a review to ask how I liked this cover. I replied and then posted my review. He has since written back and below is his response about the magnets.

"Our magnets are the strength that they are in order to prevent scuffing and scratching of the vehicle's paint. On windshield covers, if the magnets holds on too strongly, the wind will move it while it's attached and the magnet itself or the grit/dirt between the magnet and the car acts as an abrasive which scratches the paint. Our magnets break away in a high wind before that damage can occur.

With that said we are always trying to find that perfect balance between the two (having a firm attachment and avoiding scuffing) so it is great to hear this feedback and I will pass it on to our design team so we can look into adjusting magnet strength."

UPDATE March 2, 2015 - I put this cover on before a snowstorm I had last night. Although the cover stayed in place, I would not do this again. When I went to remove the cover this morning, it was like peeling tape off my windshield and car because ice had formed underneath the cover. There was probably some melting going on that seeped under the cover which caused this. However, this is excellent for keeping frost off the windshield, I just can't recommend keeping it on if it's going to snow.

title: Degreaser worked exceptionally well for my use
text:
I originally requested this product for review because I wanted to remove gunk and grease that some door edge guard left on my car doors. However, after I got the product, the instructions said not to use on motorcycles or glass and that some surfaces like aluminum alloys, plastic or painted surfaces are inherently sensitive to alkaline cleaners.

I called technical support at the company and was told to definitely not use it on the painted surface of my car because the technician felt it would surely damage the paint or finish. In fact he recommended a certain Spray 9 degreaser for that job. I then asked him if I could use it on plastics (even though it says some plastics might be sensitive). He did say that because there were so many plastics on the market, I would have to spot test it to see.

Therefore, I decided to take a chance and try this cleaner on a plastic grain shovel I have. I use this shovel for snow and was told by well-meaning neighbors to grease it up so the snow would fall off easily (that never worked). For two winters, I tried different greases on the shovel that caused such severe discoloration and tackiness that no amount of dawn, soap and water, or scrubbing with an abrasive sponge would clean. I had given up on this shovel because it had so much grease and I felt it would never be clean again.

I decided to spot test Grez-Off on the bottom of this shovel and noticing there was no bad reaction I sprayed the entire shovel and immediately used a light sponge to wipe (no hard rubbing required) and then rinse off the grease using a garden hose. The shovel looks brand new. I am actually shocked at how exceptionally well this grease came off when at the end of two winters I've tried to clean it with absolutely no success and lots strenuous scrubbing.

Of course, I followed the instructions on the back of the product precisely and because of these warnings I safely used the product outside. According to the instructions, Grez-Off is a powerful biodegradable degreaser that requires:
- the application surface to be cool
- the solution should be sprayed on full strength allowing it to penetrate the grease but NEVER allowing it to dry
- the surface should be immediately rinsed with water
- the operator should not inhale and protective gloves should be used

title: Better than most ice scrapers but still falls short of perfection
text:
I purchased the two-pack of these because I was tired of the different plastic ice scrapers I had that didn't do a good job on hard ice.

From September to April I have to scrap my car windows almost daily. This scraper is one of the better tools because there are three different scraping positions. You can scrape in the position shown (although I had trouble keeping it in that position), you can fold the two larger blades back to expose only the smaller blade, or you can fold all the blades in front for a stronger scraping action (although sometimes the ice gets caught between the different blades forcing them to separate a bit which means you need to clear the ice to continue).

This is the best scraper I used so far because it scrapes away thicker ice easily when in the reinforced position (with all blades out front). It also works well, but not great, to dislodge the thick concrete ice I get on my windshield.

I feel this product could be improved by making the blades stronger and have a locking mechanism that keeps the blades in the "stand-like" position (like shown in picture) and in the reinforced position (with all blades out front). Because the blades are slightly pliable and not as firm as a thick steel knife, scraping away ice is still not as easy as wiping away snow from a windshield but it is a whole lot better with this tool. One other issue I found is that the blade only scrapes half of its length (so if you use the small blade only what's in the center gets scraped away, meaning you'll have more passes).

However, this is still a worthwhile purchase for me because it's a lot easier to scrape away the ice with this tool than any other scraper I tried before.

Note: using in bathroom and car I’ve had no issue with streaking… But in direct sunlight on front windshield- I’ve noticed a slight milky film?!! It’s only present here.. under certain sunlight- but, A bit disheartening.

Bottom line these need a controlled temperature environment- like any premoistened wipes would. So leave in car during cooler temps only- especially since car interior can reach overly high heat! These may have a film/buildup seen under direct sunlight
-I had no issue removing film with vinegar/h2o mix. But I’ll be keeping in guest bathroom so it encourages me to use often!

The towelette wipes themselves are strong enough and create minimal shedding..70 for $11 is a higher price point then window cleaner/paper towels- but it’s paying for convenience and in guest bath it can be helpful!! Hoping info can help make your decision.. stay safe everyone.

title: Great for your older “teen cars!!”

title: Separates in half for easy storage..!!
